project.name: esport-tycoon
project.description: A deterministic esports organization management simulation in which the player develops a performer collective, plans weekly activities, handles incidents, manages organization resources, and progresses through marked seasons.

nodes.name: Talent Management
nodes.summary: This domain creates and represents the performers who make up a collective, including their six skills, age curve, languages, traits, and changing energy, morale, and form. It also provides stable information fog so player-facing observations reveal bounded ranges instead of exact hidden ratings.

businessRules: Performer generation draws all randomness from an injected deterministic RNG and consumes stats in a fixed order.
Stat and floating-state values are normalized to their declared bounds; performer state changes cannot escape those scales.
An observed stat range must contain the true value and remains stable for the same performer, stat, and observation quality.
Collective morale combines the group mean with the worst member so one unhappy performer is visible without wholly defining the group.
crossDomainInteractions: Weekly Operations selects activity participants from the collective and changes performer state.
Incident Management targets eligible performers and can change their stats, energy, morale, or form.
Simulation and Content Operations supplies origin profiles and reproducible seeds used to generate collectives.

nodes.name: Weekly Operations
nodes.summary: This domain is the deterministic time loop of a run: a finite pool of weekly attention slots is spent on planned activities, participants pay energy, and effects land on people or the organization. Multi-week advancement keeps executing weeks until the plan runs out or a decision-worthy stop condition occurs.

businessRules: A week is a pure transition of the supplied state, plan, activity mask, season calendar, and RNG stream.
Activities spend the organization slot pool, apply only to their declared participants, charge energy, and apply their closed-union effects.
Threshold stops occur only on a downward crossing measured from the start of the current week.
Advancement stops when something requires a decision rather than silently continuing through it.
crossDomainInteractions: Talent Management supplies the collective and receives activity and recovery changes.
Organization Economy supplies the weekly slot pool and receives money, audience, and reputation effects.
Incident Management can interrupt advancement with a pending incident.
Season Calendar provides each week marking and delegates active-season time progression to this domain.

nodes.name: Incident Management
nodes.summary: This domain turns authored incident content into deterministic interruptions with an eligible target, presented choices, consequences, and cooldowns. Selection and resolution are pure state transitions so a run can pause on a pending incident and replay the same outcome from serialized state.

businessRules: Only targets satisfying incident eligibility conditions may be selected.
Incident selection is cadence-gated, weighted, and driven by the injected RNG rather than caller choice.
Resolving an incident applies exactly the selected choice effects, installs its cooldown, and clears the pending incident.
Incident effects are restricted to declared performer-state, stat, form, and organization-money effect kinds.
crossDomainInteractions: Weekly Operations evaluates incident selection while advancing and stops when an incident needs a choice.
Talent Management provides candidate targets and receives performer consequences.
Organization Economy receives incident money consequences.
Simulation and Content Operations loads authored incidents and their category and trait multipliers.

nodes.name: Organization Economy
nodes.summary: This domain owns the organization ledger and attention capacity: money, audience, reputation, and the weekly slot pool. It applies declared deltas while clamping bounded measures and converts audience size into scaled reach for audience-sensitive outcomes.

businessRules: The organization ledger is kept separate from the performer collective because financial and people state have different failure modes.
Money changes by the exact declared amount, including positive and negative deltas.
Reputation stays on the inclusive 0 to 100 scale.
Audience-scaled income reaches half of its declared base at the configured half-reach audience threshold.
crossDomainInteractions: Weekly Operations spends organization slots and applies money, audience, and reputation activity effects.
Incident Management can apply money consequences from a selected choice.

nodes.name: Season Calendar
nodes.summary: This domain builds and advances a marked season calendar from a season template, tracks an active or completed season, and evaluates season goals from recorded contest facts. It also owns the explicit transition from a completed season into the next season so calendar generation and RNG continuation remain deterministic.

businessRules: Calendar markings are allocated within the inclusive ranges declared by the season template.
Season progression preserves the run RNG state so the same state and plan replay the same calendar and weekly results.
A minimum-contest-wins goal is evaluated from contest facts recorded against the season.
Starting the next season is a separate lifecycle transition from completing the current season.
crossDomainInteractions: Weekly Operations consumes the generated calendar markings and executes the weeks advanced by an active season.
Simulation and Content Operations validates and loads season templates as typed inputs, while season execution remains owned by core consumers.

nodes.name: Simulation and Content Operations
nodes.summary: This domain provides the headless simulation harness and the repository content gate around the pure core. The shared loader reads authored activities, incidents, origins, and season templates into typed inputs; the week-horizon harness consumes the first three, while season templates remain available to core season consumers.

businessRules: The core reads no files; the harness is responsible for turning the content tree into typed core inputs.
Simulation runs are driven by explicit scenarios, policies, and seeds so results can be reproduced.
Authored content remains data under the content tree rather than executable game logic.
The content validation command checks schemas and referential integrity before content is accepted.
crossDomainInteractions: It supplies activities and origin profiles to Talent Management and Weekly Operations.
It supplies incident definitions and weighting multipliers to Incident Management.
It supplies season templates to Season Calendar and reports deterministic run outcomes.

nodes.name: Generate Performer
nodes.summary: Creates one deterministic performer profile from an origin, generation parameters, trait options, and an injected RNG.

nodes.name: Read Origin Profile
nodes.summary: Use the supplied origin profile for names, handles, primary language, second-language chances, and talent density.

nodes.name: Draw Performer Identity
nodes.summary: Choose the performer identity fields from the supplied origin data through the injected RNG.

nodes.name: Generate Bounded Stats
nodes.summary: Generate the six ordered skills and normalize them to the performer stat scale.

nodes.name: Finalize Performer State
nodes.summary: Return the performer with generated traits, languages, hidden values, and bounded floating state.

nodes.name: Observe Performer
nodes.summary: Produces stable, bounded stat ranges that communicate uncertainty without exposing a performer’s exact hidden values.

nodes.name: Clamp Observation Quality
nodes.summary: Normalize the requested observation quality to the supported range.

nodes.name: Derive Stable Stat Error
nodes.summary: Derive per-stat uncertainty from the performer seed and stat key so repeated views do not reroll information.

nodes.name: Return Truth-Containing Ranges
nodes.summary: Return bounded ranges for all observed skills, each guaranteed to contain the true value.

nodes.name: Execute Week Plan
nodes.summary: Executes the activities assigned to one week, spending attention slots and applying participant and organization consequences.

nodes.name: Read Week Marking
nodes.summary: Resolve the current calendar marking and week kind supplied for this week.

nodes.name: Recover Performer Energy
nodes.summary: Apply the declared weekly energy recovery before planned work is evaluated.

nodes.name: Evaluate Planned Activities
nodes.summary: Walk the planned activity block and determine whether slots, targets, and energy allow each item to run.

nodes.name: Spend Slots and Energy
nodes.summary: Charge the organization slot pool and the participating performers for each activity that runs.

nodes.name: Apply Activity Effects
nodes.summary: Apply declared stat, energy, morale, money, audience, or reputation effects to the appropriate targets.

nodes.name: Return Week Result
nodes.summary: Return the updated run state together with executed or skipped activity outcomes and any stop reason.

nodes.name: Advance Weekly Run
nodes.summary: Walks successive weeks under one plan until advancement reaches a player-decision boundary or exhausts the planned block.

nodes.name: Restore Run RNG
nodes.summary: Restore the deterministic random stream carried by the serialized run state.

nodes.name: Execute Current Week
nodes.summary: Run the current week against the supplied plan, mask, and season calendar.

nodes.name: Evaluate Threshold Crossings
nodes.summary: Compare week-start and week-end energy and morale to detect configured downward crossings.

nodes.name: Evaluate Decision Stops
nodes.summary: Stop for an incident, threshold, skipped activity, exhausted block, or other declared reason that needs attention.

nodes.name: Continue or Return
nodes.summary: Advance to another week only when no decision stop has fired; otherwise return the updated state and reason.

nodes.name: Select Weekly Incident
nodes.summary: Chooses whether an authored incident becomes pending this week and deterministically selects its eligible target.

nodes.name: Check Cadence Gate
nodes.summary: Determine whether the incident cadence permits a selection attempt in the current week.

nodes.name: Filter Active Cooldowns
nodes.summary: Exclude incident candidates that remain blocked by their installed cooldown.

nodes.name: Find Eligible Targets
nodes.summary: Evaluate incident conditions against the collective and return only eligible performer identifiers.

nodes.name: Weight Incident Candidates
nodes.summary: Apply authored base weights together with category and trait multipliers.

nodes.name: Install Pending Incident
nodes.summary: Use the incident RNG stream to choose the candidate and target and persist them as the pending interruption.

nodes.name: Resolve Pending Incident
nodes.summary: Applies the selected choice of a pending incident, records its cooldown, and resumes the run without caller-invented consequences.

nodes.name: Validate Pending Choice
nodes.summary: Resolve the requested choice against the currently pending authored incident and target.

nodes.name: Apply Performer Consequences
nodes.summary: Apply declared stat, energy, morale, or form effects to the targeted performer or collective.

nodes.name: Apply Money Consequences
nodes.summary: Apply any declared money effect to the organization ledger.

nodes.name: Set Cooldown and Clear Pending
nodes.summary: Install the incident cooldown and clear the pending interruption in the returned run state.

nodes.name: Apply Organization Change
nodes.summary: Applies a declared money, audience, reputation, or slot change to the organization ledger.

nodes.name: Read Declared Deltas
nodes.summary: Read the resource changes carried by the organization change value.

nodes.name: Change Money Balance
nodes.summary: Move the balance by the exact positive or negative money amount.

nodes.name: Change Audience and Reputation
nodes.summary: Apply audience and reputation deltas while keeping bounded measures within their supported scales.

nodes.name: Return Updated Organization
nodes.summary: Return a new organization value with its updated ledger and attention capacity.

nodes.name: Calculate Audience-Scaled Reach
nodes.summary: Converts the organization audience into the reach multiplier used for audience-sensitive income or effects.

nodes.name: Read Audience
nodes.summary: Read the current organization audience used by the scaling rule.

nodes.name: Apply Half-Reach Curve
nodes.summary: Apply the configured curve whose half point is the declared audience half-reach constant.

nodes.name: Return Reach Factor
nodes.summary: Return the deterministic multiplier for the caller’s audience-scaled outcome.

nodes.name: Start Season
nodes.summary: Creates the first active season and its deterministic marked calendar from a season template and run RNG state.

nodes.name: Read Season Template
nodes.summary: Read the season length, marking ranges, and goal configuration from the supplied template.

nodes.name: Restore Calendar RNG
nodes.summary: Restore the deterministic RNG state used to allocate the season calendar.

nodes.name: Allocate Week Markings
nodes.summary: Assign marked week kinds within the inclusive count ranges declared by the template.

nodes.name: Create Active Season
nodes.summary: Return an active season with its calendar, current position, goal state, and continued RNG state.

nodes.name: Advance Active Season
nodes.summary: Advances an active season through weekly operations and transitions it to completed when its calendar is exhausted.

nodes.name: Read Active Calendar Position
nodes.summary: Read the active season’s current calendar entry and accumulated week-kind counts.

nodes.name: Delegate Week Advancement
nodes.summary: Call weekly advancement with the season calendar, run state, plan, and options.

nodes.name: Capture Advance Result
nodes.summary: Store the returned run state, stop reason, and deterministic RNG continuation.

nodes.name: Update Season Progress
nodes.summary: Advance the season cursor and week-kind accounting for each completed calendar week.

nodes.name: Complete or Return Active Season
nodes.summary: Return an updated active season unless the final calendar week was consumed, in which case return a completed season.

nodes.name: Record Season Contest Fact
nodes.summary: Records a contest result against the active season so its minimum-wins goal can be evaluated from explicit facts.

nodes.name: Accept Contest Fact
nodes.summary: Accept the declared contest outcome for the current season.

nodes.name: Update Win Accounting
nodes.summary: Update the season facts used by the minimum-contest-wins goal.

nodes.name: Return Season with Fact
nodes.summary: Return the season state with the contest fact preserved for later completion evaluation.

nodes.name: Start Next Season
nodes.summary: Transitions from a completed season to a new active season using the next template while preserving deterministic lifecycle state.

nodes.name: Require Completed Season
nodes.summary: Use the completed season lifecycle state as the source for the next-season transition.

nodes.name: Carry Forward RNG State
nodes.summary: Restore the RNG continuation stored by the completed season.

nodes.name: Read Next Template
nodes.summary: Read the next season’s marking ranges and goal configuration.

nodes.name: Generate Next Calendar
nodes.summary: Deterministically allocate the next season calendar from the carried RNG state.

nodes.name: Return Next Active Season
nodes.summary: Return the newly active season with reset progress and its own goal tracking.

nodes.name: Run Deterministic Simulation
nodes.summary: Runs a headless scenario under a selected planning policy and produces a reproducible report from typed repository content.

nodes.name: Load Typed Content
nodes.summary: Read activities, origins, incidents, multipliers, and season templates from the repository content tree.

nodes.name: Build Scenario
nodes.summary: Use the scenario module to assemble the starting collective, organization, run state, and seed inputs.

nodes.name: Select Planning Policy
nodes.summary: Use the policy module to choose the deterministic weekly plans supplied to the core.

nodes.name: Execute Headless Run
nodes.summary: Use the run module to drive weekly and season transitions without a UI shell.

nodes.name: Emit Simulation Report
nodes.summary: Use the report module to present the resulting deterministic simulation outcomes.

nodes.name: Validate Content Tree
nodes.summary: Runs the repository content gate so authored data satisfies its schemas and cross-file references before simulation or gameplay consumes it.

nodes.name: Discover Content Files
nodes.summary: Enumerate authored data under the repository content tree.

nodes.name: Validate Against Schemas
nodes.summary: Check each content document against the applicable content schema.

nodes.name: Check Referential Integrity
nodes.summary: Verify that identifiers and references across content documents resolve consistently.

nodes.name: Report Validation Result
nodes.summary: Exit successfully only when the content set passes the validation gate and report actionable failures otherwise.

edges.description: Collectives and performer state are the participants and mutable people state of weekly activities.
Weekly activities spend attention slots and apply money, audience, and reputation effects to the organization.
Week advancement evaluates deterministic incident selection and stops when a pending incident requires a choice.
Incident eligibility selects performer targets and resolved choices can change their skills or floating state.
Incident choices can apply authored money consequences to the organization ledger.
An active season supplies the marked calendar to weekly advancement and consumes the resulting progress and stop reasons.
The harness loads origin profiles and supplies seeded inputs for reproducible performer and collective generation.
Scenarios and policies drive the pure weekly loop with typed activities and explicit seeds.
Authored incident definitions and weighting multipliers are loaded as typed inputs for incident selection and resolution.
The shared content loader exposes validated season templates; the week-horizon harness does not execute the season lifecycle.
